edition: Hebrew–English column (Literal-Smooth, Rabbinic Priority) of the Saints.Bible Parallel Reader
source_hebrew: Westminster Leningrad Codex (pointed text via Sefaria)

13:1.hebrew: בֶּן־שָׁנָה שָׁאוּל בְּמָלְכוֹ וּשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים מָלַךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
13:1.english: Saul was […] years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel two years.
13:1.editorial_note: The Masoretic Text reads literally ‘a son of a year’ in the usual place for the accession age and gives ‘two years’ for the reign. The age is left unresolved. Rashi also reads the opening as referring to Saul’s first year as king.

17:12.hebrew: וְדָוִד בֶּן־אִישׁ אֶפְרָתִי הַזֶּה מִבֵּית לֶחֶם יְהוּדָה וּשְׁמוֹ יִשַׁי וְלוֹ שְׁמֹנָה בָנִים וְהָאִישׁ בִּימֵי שָׁאוּל זָקֵן בָּא בַאֲנָשִׁים׃
17:12.english: Now David was the son of an Ephrathite from Bethlehem in Judah named Jesse. Jesse had eight sons. In Saul’s days he was old and counted among the leading men.
17:12.editorial_note: The last Hebrew phrase literally says ‘coming among men.’ The rendering follows Rashi’s understanding that Jesse was numbered among men of standing.

17:13.hebrew: וַיֵּלְכוּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת בְּנֵי־יִשַׁי הַגְּדֹלִים הָלְכוּ אַחֲרֵי־שָׁאוּל לַמִּלְחָמָה וְשֵׁם שְׁלֹשֶׁת בָּנָיו אֲשֶׁר הָלְכוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָה אֱלִיאָב הַבְּכוֹר וּמִשְׁנֵהוּ אֲבִינָדָב וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁי שַׁמָּה׃
17:13.english: Jesse’s three eldest sons had followed Saul to battle. The three sons who went to battle were Eliab the firstborn, Abinadab the second, and Shammah the third.

17:14.hebrew: וְדָוִד הוּא הַקָּטָן וּשְׁלֹשָׁה הַגְּדֹלִים הָלְכוּ אַחֲרֵי שָׁאוּל׃
17:14.english: David was the youngest, and the three eldest followed Saul.

17:15.hebrew: וְדָוִד הֹלֵךְ וָשָׁב מֵעַל שָׁאוּל לִרְעוֹת אֶת־צֹאן אָבִיו בֵּית־לָחֶם׃
17:15.english: David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s sheep in Bethlehem.

17:16.hebrew: וַיִּגַּשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הַשְׁכֵּם וְהַעֲרֵב וַיִּתְיַצֵּב אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם׃
17:16.english: For forty days the Philistine drew near and took his stand, morning and evening.

17:17.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר יִשַׁי לְדָוִד בְּנוֹ קַח־נָא לְאַחֶיךָ אֵיפַת הַקָּלִיא הַזֶּה וַעֲשָׂרָה לֶחֶם הַזֶּה וְהָרֵץ הַמַּחֲנֶה לְאַחֶיךָ׃
17:17.english: Jesse said to his son David, “Please take an ephah of this roasted grain and these ten loaves to your brothers. Hurry to the camp with them for your brothers.

17:18.hebrew: וְאֵת עֲשֶׂרֶת חֲרִצֵי הֶחָלָב הָאֵלֶּה תָּבִיא לְשַׂר־הָאָלֶף וְאֶת־אַחֶיךָ תִּפְקֹד לְשָׁלוֹם וְאֶת־עֲרֻבָּתָם תִּקָּח׃
17:18.english: Take these ten cheeses to the commander of the thousand. See how your brothers are faring and bring back word of their welfare.”
17:18.editorial_note: The final expression can refer to taking a pledge or token. The rendering follows Targum Jonathan and Rashi, who understand it as bringing back assurance that the brothers are well.

17:19.hebrew: וְשָׁאוּל וְהֵמָּה וְכָל־אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֵמֶק הָאֵלָה נִלְחָמִים עִם־פְּלִשְׁתִּים׃
17:19.english: Saul, the brothers, and all Israel’s men were in the Valley of Elah, fighting the Philistines.

17:20.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁכֵּם דָּוִד בַּבֹּקֶר וַיִּטֹּשׁ אֶת־הַצֹּאן עַל־שֹׁמֵר וַיִּשָּׂא וַיֵּלֶךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּהוּ יִשָׁי וַיָּבֹא הַמַּעְגָּלָה וְהַחַיִל הַיֹּצֵא אֶל־הַמַּעֲרָכָה וְהֵרֵעוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָה׃
17:20.english: David rose early in the morning, left the sheep with a keeper, picked up the provisions, and went as Jesse had commanded him. He reached the camp perimeter as the troops were going out to the battle line and raising the battle cry.

17:21.hebrew: וַתַּעֲרֹךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּפְלִשְׁתִּים מַעֲרָכָה לִקְרַאת מַעֲרָכָה׃
17:21.english: Israel and the Philistines drew up for battle, one line facing the other.

17:22.hebrew: וַיִּטֹּשׁ דָּוִד אֶת־הַכֵּלִים מֵעָלָיו עַל־יַד שׁוֹמֵר הַכֵּלִים וַיָּרָץ הַמַּעֲרָכָה וַיָּבֹא וַיִּשְׁאַל לְאֶחָיו לְשָׁלוֹם׃
17:22.english: David left the gear he was carrying with the baggage keeper and ran to the battle line. When he reached his brothers, he asked how they were.

17:23.hebrew: וְהוּא מְדַבֵּר עִמָּם וְהִנֵּה אִישׁ הַבֵּנַיִם עוֹלֶה גָּלְיָת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי שְׁמוֹ מִגַּת ממערות [מִמַּעַרְכוֹת] פְּלִשְׁתִּים וַיְדַבֵּר כַּדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וַיִּשְׁמַע דָּוִד׃
17:23.english: While David was speaking with them, the champion came up from the Philistine battle lines. His name was Goliath, the Philistine from Gath. He spoke the same words as before, and David heard him.
17:23.editorial_note: ‘Battle lines’ follows the Masoretic qere (the reading tradition). The pointed witness also preserves the ketiv (the written form).

17:24.hebrew: וְכֹל אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּרְאוֹתָם אֶת־הָאִישׁ וַיָּנֻסוּ מִפָּנָיו וַיִּירְאוּ מְאֹד׃
17:24.english: When all Israel’s men saw the man, they fled from him in great fear.

17:25.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַרְּאִיתֶם הָאִישׁ הָעֹלֶה הַזֶּה כִּי לְחָרֵף אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל עֹלֶה וְהָיָה הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יַכֶּנּוּ יַעְשְׁרֶנּוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ עֹשֶׁר גָּדוֹל וְאֶת־בִּתּוֹ יִתֶּן־לוֹ וְאֵת בֵּית אָבִיו יַעֲשֶׂה חָפְשִׁי בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל׃
17:25.english: Israel’s men said, “Do you see this man coming up? He comes up to defy Israel. The king will give great wealth to whoever strikes him down. He will give him his daughter and make his father’s household free in Israel.”

17:26.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל־הָאֲנָשִׁים הָעֹמְדִים עִמּוֹ לֵאמֹר מַה־יֵּעָשֶׂה לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יַכֶּה אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הַלָּז וְהֵסִיר חֶרְפָּה מֵעַל יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי מִי הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הֶעָרֵל הַזֶּה כִּי חֵרֵף מַעַרְכוֹת אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים׃
17:26.english: David asked the men standing with him, “What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and removes the disgrace from Israel? Who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the battle lines of the living God?”

17:27.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ הָעָם כַּדָּבָר הַזֶּה לֵאמֹר כֹּה יֵעָשֶׂה לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יַכֶּנּוּ׃
17:27.english: The people gave him the same answer. “That is what will be done for the man who strikes him down.”

17:28.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁמַע אֱלִיאָב אָחִיו הַגָּדוֹל בְּדַבְּרוֹ אֶל־הָאֲנָשִׁים וַיִּחַר־אַף אֱלִיאָב בְּדָוִד וַיֹּאמֶר לָמָּה־זֶּה יָרַדְתָּ וְעַל־מִי נָטַשְׁתָּ מְעַט הַצֹּאן הָהֵנָּה בַּמִּדְבָּר אֲנִי יָדַעְתִּי אֶת־זְדֹנְךָ וְאֵת רֹעַ לְבָבֶךָ כִּי לְמַעַן רְאוֹת הַמִּלְחָמָה יָרָדְתָּ׃
17:28.english: Eliab, his eldest brother, heard him talking to the men. He grew angry with David and said, “Why did you come down? With whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil in your heart. You came down to watch the battle.”

17:29.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד מֶה עָשִׂיתִי עָתָּה הֲלוֹא דָּבָר הוּא׃
17:29.english: David said, “What have I done now? Was it not just a word?”

17:30.hebrew: וַיִּסֹּב מֵאֶצְלוֹ אֶל־מוּל אַחֵר וַיֹּאמֶר כַּדָּבָר הַזֶּה וַיְשִׁבֻהוּ הָעָם דָּבָר כַּדָּבָר הָרִאשׁוֹן׃
17:30.english: He turned away from Eliab to someone else and said the same thing. The people gave him the same answer as before.

17:31.hebrew: וַיְּשָּׁמְעוּ הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר דָּוִד וַיַּגִּדוּ לִפְנֵי־שָׁאוּל וַיִּקָּחֵהוּ׃
17:31.english: People heard what David had said and reported it to Saul, who sent for him.

17:41.hebrew: וַיֵּלֶךְ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הֹלֵךְ וְקָרֵב אֶל־דָּוִד וְהָאִישׁ נֹשֵׂא הַצִּנָּה לְפָנָיו׃
17:41.english: The Philistine drew nearer and nearer to David, with his shield-bearer ahead of him.

17:50.hebrew: וַיֶּחֱזַק דָּוִד מִן־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי בַּקֶּלַע וּבָאֶבֶן וַיַּךְ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַיְמִיתֵהוּ וְחֶרֶב אֵין בְּיַד־דָּוִד׃
17:50.english: David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone. He struck the Philistine and killed him, though there was no sword in David’s hand.

17:55.hebrew: וְכִרְאוֹת שָׁאוּל אֶת־דָּוִד יֹצֵא לִקְרַאת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי אָמַר אֶל־אַבְנֵר שַׂר הַצָּבָא בֶּן־מִי־זֶה הַנַּעַר אַבְנֵר וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְנֵר חֵי־נַפְשְׁךָ הַמֶּלֶךְ אִם־יָדָעְתִּי׃
17:55.english: When Saul saw David go out to meet the Philistine, he asked Abner, his army commander, “Abner, whose son is this young man?” Abner answered, “As your soul lives, O king, I do not know.”

17:56.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁאַל אַתָּה בֶּן־מִי־זֶה הָעָלֶם׃
17:56.english: The king said, “Find out whose son the young man is.”

17:57.hebrew: וּכְשׁוּב דָּוִד מֵהַכּוֹת אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַיִּקַּח אֹתוֹ אַבְנֵר וַיְבִאֵהוּ לִפְנֵי שָׁאוּל וְרֹאשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי בְּיָדוֹ׃
17:57.english: When David came back from striking down the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul. The Philistine’s head was in David’s hand.

17:58.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו שָׁאוּל בֶּן־מִי אַתָּה הַנָּעַר וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד בֶּן־עַבְדְּךָ יִשַׁי בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי׃
17:58.english: Saul asked him, “Whose son are you, young man?” David answered, “I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem.”

18:1.hebrew: וַיְהִי כְּכַלֹּתוֹ לְדַבֵּר אֶל־שָׁאוּל וְנֶפֶשׁ יְהוֹנָתָן נִקְשְׁרָה בְּנֶפֶשׁ דָּוִד ויאהבו [וַיֶּאֱהָבֵהוּ] יְהוֹנָתָן כְּנַפְשׁוֹ׃
18:1.english: When David finished speaking to Saul, Jonathan’s soul was bound to David’s soul, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
18:1.editorial_note: The English follows the Masoretic qere for ‘and he loved him.’ The pointed witness also preserves the ketiv.

18:2.hebrew: וַיִּקָּחֵהוּ שָׁאוּל בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וְלֹא נְתָנוֹ לָשׁוּב בֵּית אָבִיו׃
18:2.english: That day Saul took David and would not let him return to his father’s house.

18:3.hebrew: וַיִּכְרֹת יְהוֹנָתָן וְדָוִד בְּרִית בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ אֹתוֹ כְּנַפְשׁוֹ׃
18:3.english: Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as his own soul.

18:4.hebrew: וַיִּתְפַּשֵּׁט יְהוֹנָתָן אֶת־הַמְּעִיל אֲשֶׁר עָלָיו וַיִּתְּנֵהוּ לְדָוִד וּמַדָּיו וְעַד־חַרְבּוֹ וְעַד־קַשְׁתּוֹ וְעַד־חֲגֹרוֹ׃
18:4.english: Jonathan took off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his garments, his sword, his bow, and his belt.

18:5.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵא דָוִד בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁלָחֶנּוּ שָׁאוּל יַשְׂכִּיל וַיְשִׂמֵהוּ שָׁאוּל עַל אַנְשֵׁי הַמִּלְחָמָה וַיִּיטַב בְּעֵינֵי כָל־הָעָם וְגַם בְּעֵינֵי עַבְדֵי שָׁאוּל׃
18:5.english: David went out wherever Saul sent him and had success. Saul put him in command of the fighting men. This pleased all the people and Saul’s servants as well.

18:10.hebrew: וַיְהִי מִמָּחֳרָת וַתִּצְלַח רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים רָעָה אֶל־שָׁאוּל וַיִּתְנַבֵּא בְתוֹךְ־הַבַּיִת וְדָוִד מְנַגֵּן בְּיָדוֹ כְּיוֹם בְּיוֹם וְהַחֲנִית בְּיַד־שָׁאוּל׃
18:10.english: The next day an evil spirit from God rushed upon Saul, and he raved inside the house. David was playing with his hand, as he did each day, and Saul had the spear in his hand.
18:10.editorial_note: ‘Raved’ follows Targum Jonathan and Rashi. The Hebrew uses the verb otherwise used for prophesying.

18:11.hebrew: וַיָּטֶל שָׁאוּל אֶת־הַחֲנִית וַיֹּאמֶר אַכֶּה בְדָוִד וּבַקִּיר וַיִּסֹּב דָּוִד מִפָּנָיו פַּעֲמָיִם׃
18:11.english: Saul hurled the spear, saying, “I will pin David to the wall.” David got out of his way twice.

18:17.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־דָּוִד הִנֵּה בִתִּי הַגְּדוֹלָה מֵרַב אֹתָהּ אֶתֶּן־לְךָ לְאִשָּׁה אַךְ הֱיֵה־לִּי לְבֶן־חַיִל וְהִלָּחֵם מִלְחֲמוֹת יְהוָה וְשָׁאוּל אָמַר אַל־תְּהִי יָדִי בּוֹ וּתְהִי־בוֹ יַד־פְּלִשְׁתִּים׃
18:17.english: Saul said to David, “Here is my elder daughter Merab. I will give her to you as a wife. Only be a valiant warrior for me and fight YHWH’s battles.” Saul said to himself, “Let my hand not be against him. Let the hand of the Philistines be against him.”

18:18.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל־שָׁאוּל מִי אָנֹכִי וּמִי חַיַּי מִשְׁפַּחַת אָבִי בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי־אֶהְיֶה חָתָן לַמֶּלֶךְ׃
18:18.english: David said to Saul, “Who am I? What is my life, or my father’s family in Israel, that I should become the king’s son-in-law?”
18:18.editorial_note: The Hebrew is compressed and retains ‘my life’ as well as ‘my father’s family.’ The question concerns David’s standing and that of his household.

18:19.hebrew: וַיְהִי בְּעֵת תֵּת אֶת־מֵרַב בַּת־שָׁאוּל לְדָוִד וְהִיא נִתְּנָה לְעַדְרִיאֵל הַמְּחֹלָתִי לְאִשָּׁה׃
18:19.english: When the time came for Saul’s daughter Merab to be given to David, she was given instead to Adriel the Meholathite as his wife.

18:30.hebrew: וַיֵּצְאוּ שָׂרֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיְהִי מִדֵּי צֵאתָם שָׂכַל דָּוִד מִכֹּל עַבְדֵי שָׁאוּל וַיִּיקַר שְׁמוֹ מְאֹד׃
18:30.english: The Philistine commanders went out, and every time they went out, David was more successful than any of Saul’s servants. His name came to be held in great honor.

23:12.hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד הֲיַסְגִּרוּ בַּעֲלֵי קְעִילָה אֹתִי וְאֶת־אֲנָשַׁי בְּיַד־שָׁאוּל וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה יַסְגִּירוּ׃
23:12.english: David asked, “Will Keilah’s masters deliver me and my men into Saul’s hand?” YHWH answered, “They will deliver you up.”
